anz_items.headline: Impact Minerals goes to shareholders for A$4.1 million to push its high purity alumina plans along
anz_items.detail: The Perth-based explorer launched a one-for-four renounceable rights issue priced at A$0.032 per share - a 22 per cent discount to its last close of A$0.041 - partially underwritten to A$1.5 million by Mahe Capital, with two free attaching options for every three new shares and proceeds directed at the Lake Hope High Purity Alumina Project plus its Broken Hill and Lake Irwin ground.

anz_items.headline: Sovereign AI infrastructure play SCX.ai lands on the ASX boards with A$40 million in fresh capital
anz_items.detail: SCX.ai Holdings began trading on 21 August 2026 under the ticker SCX after completing a A$40 million initial public offering at A$0.30 per share, with the company reporting contracted annual recurring revenue up 21 per cent as demand for domestic AI cloud capacity accelerates.

uk_items.headline: Vast Resources returns to AIM with a GBP 7.8 million raise behind a Tajik gold reverse takeover
uk_items.detail: The mining company completed its reverse takeover of Gulf International Minerals and was readmitted to AIM at 8:00am on 19 August 2026 after raising roughly GBP 7.85 million through a placing, subscription and oversubscribed retail offer, giving it a 49 per cent interest in a Tajik joint venture holding four gold mines.

abc_item.headline: Central Coast baby becomes the first person anywhere to get a precision drug for a lethal genetic epilepsy
abc_item.detail: Eight-month-old Bohdi Higginson, who has KCNT1-related catastrophic epilepsy and recorded 74 seizures on his worst day, received his first dose at the Children's Hospital at Westmead on 21 April and had his last seizure three days later, in a world first delivered through the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network's new innovative therapies pathway.

summaries.anz: Australasian issuance this week was dominated by small caps topping up the tank rather than blue chips raising serious money, with Sports Entertainment Group's A$14.6 million placement the largest deal on the board and the only one tied to a genuine acquisition - the NZ$130 million purchase of MediaWorks. Everything else sat well under A$5 million and leaned heavily on materials and deep tech, with Impact Minerals going renounceable for A$4.1 million on high purity alumina and Sparc Technologies pairing a placement with a share purchase plan to commercialise its graphene coatings additive. The one genuinely new listing, SCX.ai's A$40 million IPO at 30 cents, was the standout for scale and showed that sovereign AI infrastructure can still clear a bookbuild when mining juniors are grinding for a couple of million. A common thread across the smaller raises was the retail sweetener - share purchase plans and free attaching options used to keep existing holders from being diluted out quietly.
summaries.uk: The UK column is thin this week and skewed toward companies deciding that London is not where they want to price themselves. Nscale is chasing up to about US$3 billion in New York with a September window flagged, and Glencore is openly weighing an Australian secondary listing while it reconsiders whether its primary home still makes sense - both stories are really about valuation frustration rather than growth capital. Against those, the only actual money raised on a UK venue was Vast Resources' roughly GBP 7.8 million placing, subscription and retail offer, a modest sum that funded a reverse takeover into Tajik gold and got the company readmitted to AIM on 19 August.
summaries.rest: The rest of the world was carried almost entirely by Dangote, whose refinery locked in about US$1 billion of underwriting ahead of what would rank as Africa's biggest float - and notably kept it retail-focused on the Nigerian Exchange with no foreign listing for now. That decision has already drawn competitive interest, with the Johannesburg Stock Exchange courting Dangote for a secondary listing once the Nigerian debut is done, a reminder that African exchanges are now actively competing for the continent's marquee issuers. The only completed deal was Indian logistics group Shiprocket, which surged on debut after a roughly US$170 million offering, leaving the region as a story of one enormous pending float and one successful mid-sized one.
